get.description: Which of the sessions the repeated id parameter names (1 to 100 session ids) Dispatch holds any record of, so a page links a dispatch://agent/<session id> reference only where that conversation exists, an ended session's included: {sessions: [{session_id, title}]} in the order asked, each once, and no row for an id with no record. A record is the registry copy GET /api/v1/agents lists (whatever its age), an event the session wrote, a message targeted at it, a message or comment delivery to it, a file or image of its conversation, or an ask it follows; title is the registry copy's, null where that copy lists the session with none or does not list it. One statement answers the whole batch. No id, more than 100, a value that is no session id, or one longer than 2048 bytes, the longest session id a reference in text names, is 400 INVALID_QUERY naming the parameter; a parameter it does not take is read by nothing. It needs the person scope and admits exactly the callers GET /api/v1/agents/{session_id}/messages admits; session is the session the request acts for, as on every route.

get.description: What people wrote that Dispatch delivered to one session, newest first by at, then by id: each ask's current answer (replaced when it changed an earlier answer), each comment at its current body (edited_at when edited; a resolved comment stays), each message at its current body (edited_at when edited), a deleted comment or message in its place with deleted_at and deleted_by and an empty text, and each ask a person declined to answer, once however it arrived. It reads the ask.answered, comment.created, message.created, message.answered and ask.resolved events a person wrote whose published_destinations hold the session's own topic, the session's message deliveries the listener took (targeted and broadcast messages, handed to the running session or queued for it) and its comment deliveries (mentions) in those same two states; of an ask's resolutions it lists the decline alone, and it never lists an agent's or the system's words, a retraction, a withdrawal, another resolution, a hand-back, or a delivery to a role: route's topic. Each item names its relation to the session. A session owns an ask when it wrote the ask or follows it, and only an owner is told that an ask is its own: for a comment, replied_on_your_ask (a reply in the thread of an ask the session owns) over mentioned_you over replied_in_a_comment_thread over commented_on_a_document over commented_on_an_issue; for a message, replied_to_your_message over sent_you_a_message; for an answer, answered_your_ask for an owner and answered_an_ask for any other session; for a decline, declined_your_ask for an owner and declined_an_ask for any other session. A session that does not own the ask reads a reply in its thread by the reason that delivered it: the issue's route, its claim, a credit on its primary document, or a mention. Each item carries the ask and its whole question on an answer, on a decline and on a reply in an ask's thread, whoever asked it, and its owner, dispatch:// ref and href (null owner and ref, and /agents/<session_id>/live, for a direct message). A decline carries a kind of its own, declined, at the resolution's own time, its id the ask's, and its words in two parts: text, the person's own note, empty when they wrote none, and, on declined_your_ask alone, dispatch_words, the sentences Dispatch wrote for the asking agent; nobody chose an option, so it carries no selected. ?since= (RFC3339, default 72 hours ago; older than 7 days or in the future is 400 INVALID_QUERY) starts the window; ?max_chars= (1-100000, else 400 INVALID_QUERY) stops the list after the item whose words take the running sum past it, counting the UTF-16 units of text and, on a decline that carries them, of dispatch_words beside it, while total counts every item in the window; {session_id, since, total, items}. A session_id that is not a session id is 400 INVALID_SESSION_ID, as on the agent artifact routes. Not an authorization boundary: direct-message text already reaches every authenticated caller through GET /api/v1/events, and a person may read any session's list.

post.description: Send an issue-less targeted message to a session: {body, delivery, in_reply_to?, connected_only?}, answered once its own delivery attempt has settled, on past a client that gives up. A session the Envoy listener knows and that is not running is a recipient: the listener stores the message and hands it over when that session runs again, and the attempt is recorded queued rather than sent. A session the listener knows nothing about ("no live session <id>") is queued too: Dispatch publishes the message on that session's own subject itself, and the attempt fails with "no live session <id>" only where Dispatch has no NATS to publish on or the publish fails. connected_only asks for a session that is running now and fails the attempt with "the session is stopped", nothing stored; every later attempt of the message asks what its first asked. A model or thinking switch the session would run as its own turn - a person's own Send or Aside, not one an agent wrote for them, whose whole body is one /model or /effort line, which would otherwise apply at an unknown later time - is held to a running session at every send whether or not the request set connected_only. Under an Idempotency-Key header (as every POST and PATCH takes one), a repeat with the same request answers 201 with the message the key made and its deliveries as they stand, Idempotency-Replayed: ?1, first sending the one attempt it still owes (none yet, or one stranded past its claim) and nothing else; a listener it cannot reach is recorded on the attempt, so a repeat is answered while the listener is down. An attempt a stopped process left owed is resumed by the server's delivery sweep whether anyone asks again or not.

post.description: Open an approval ask for a document's latest version, with an optional summary, and with include_verification for the issue's Verification document beside it (409 NO_VERIFICATION_DOCUMENT when it has none), each at its own current version; the answer reviews every document the ask names. include_verification is for the issue's spec alone: on any other document, the Verification document itself included, it is 409 NOT_SPEC_DOCUMENT. A document a human approved before carries that approval on the ask (approval.approved: version, at, by). An open ask follows later versions of any document it names and waits on its agent until this route hands the same row back to a human, save that an ask waiting on the human keeps its turn, quietly, over a version a settlement writes that holds the text the ask names, byte for byte or, for a version another renderer version stored or none stamped, as Dispatch renders that text now; a version a route writes (a named version, an upload, an edit) moves it to its agent whatever text it holds. Every answer carries coverage, one line per requirement of the issue's spec with no check, or the single line `the spec marks no requirements` for a spec that marks none (GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/coverage), and none at all for a spec every requirement of which has a check; it is empty for a document that is not a spec, never names a missing plan task, and a gap refuses nothing. A coverage read that fails answers coverage_unread true and records the request all the same.

get.description: What changed between two stored versions of one document, ?from=<n>&to=<m>: {artifact_id, from, to, decision_only, unchanged, sections, blocks}, both versions read from their stored markdown with every ask block cut out, so the block index's deferred pass is never waited for. Exactly one of three holds: decision_only, true when the two stored texts differ and cut to the same text; unchanged, true when the two differ in nothing any section or block holds (the stored texts are the same, or the cut texts name nothing and are not decision-only); or sections and blocks name at least one item. sections and blocks are empty when decision_only or unchanged is true. sections is each top-level unit whose text differs, that moved, or that one version alone holds: a `##` section by heading and occurrence (the heading's text as a heading anchor reads it, without markdown's syntax and with a line break in it as a line feed; 0 for the first section of that heading, so a `##` heading with no words counts from occurrence 1), and a run of the text outside every `##` section (the title and what stands above the first `##`, or what follows a `#` heading up to the next `##`) under heading "" and occurrence 0 with its place: place before_first_section, or place after_section with after_heading and after_occurrence naming the `##` section directly before the run, in the later version for a changed, added or moved run and in the earlier for a removed one. A `#` or `##` heading that holds a line break, which is stored in setext form with no `#`, cuts the document as any heading of its level does. blocks is each typed block but an ask whose text or any attribute differs, by id and type. Each unit and block is marked changed, added or removed, and a unit whose text is the same is marked moved when its place among the document's top-level units is another: it stands outside one longest common subsequence of the two versions' orders of the units both hold, and of several that long the one kept holds the later version's earliest units, so of two units that swapped places the later version's second is moved. Both versions hold a run when both hold its text at the same place, and then, among the runs left in each version, the n-th run of one text in each is one run in both, so adding or removing one copy of a repeated run moves no other copy's match; a run the other version does not hold pairs with that version's unpaired run at the same place and is marked changed, and a run left unpaired is added or removed. A block is never marked moved. Each list holds the later version's items in its document order, a moved unit where the later version holds it, then what only the earlier holds, in its order. from and to must be positive, at most 2147483647 (the largest version number the store holds), and from below to (400 INVALID_VERSION); a version the document does not have is 404 NOT_FOUND, and a file or an image 400 NOT_DOCUMENT.

post.description: Revoke a credential grant as the caller: its approver, or the person its enrollment acts for, ends it whatever project it touches. A grant revoked by someone it does not name is 404 when it belongs to a private project the caller may not see, as an id no grant has, and 503 PROJECT_ACCESS_UNAVAILABLE while the broker cannot ask Dispatch; of the grants they may see, they end one whose approver is anyone, and any other is 403 NOT_APPROVER. A caller Dispatch calls a restricted member ends a grant only as the person its enrollment acts for: any other is 403 NOT_APPROVER, saying why. While Dispatch does not answer the broker what kind of member the caller is (a timeout, a failed connection, a gateway's 502, 503 or 504, Dispatch's own DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE or OIDC_ISSUER_UNAVAILABLE, or a 500 naming no code or INTERNAL, which Dispatch answers while its database fails), only the person the grant names as its approver ends it as an approver: every revoke through a group or as anyone then, whatever session holds the grant, and every revoke while Dispatch answers anything else the broker cannot read (a refused account, a kind the broker does not know, another code, a certificate or a name that does not resolve), is 503 MEMBER_KIND_UNCHECKABLE, revoking nothing. A grant on a person's session can still be ended then by that person, who asks Dispatch nothing; a grant on a session that acts for no person (a service's pod, a person's pod the broker no longer maps, or a machine's own session) is ended through the broker by nobody but its named approver until Dispatch answers.

get.description: The checks of the issue's Verification document in document order, each with its attributes (when, surface, run, negative_control, ci_check), the version its words last changed in and their digest, and every result recorded against it from any issue, newest first: {issue, verification_artifact_id, checks}. A check's text is its words with every link and dispatch:// reference dropped; a caller that sent Dispatch-Trees: 1 is also given text_tree, the check's whole content as the tree a reader is shown, links and references kept, and each result's observed_tree, the tree its observed text is shown as. A check's results come newest first by created_at, the time the recording transaction began, with id descending breaking a tie, and a client reading one result per check reads the first. Two results recorded in transactions that overlapped can come back in either order. Each check carries compared_with, the commits and branches its results are compared with, in the order they are asked about. For a before_merge check that is every pull request head Dispatch holds for the check's issue, each {kind: pull_request, commit, pull_request, learned_at: {at, kind}}, the kind of time being read_at when Dispatch last read that pull request from GitHub (checked_at) and updated_at when the pull request's own update time, as its newest webhook event carried it (event_at), is the later of the two. Those are the open and merged pull requests attributed to the check's issue, and the open and merged pull requests its external links name (https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>) in a repository it does not resolve to, each at the head its stored row holds now; the head of a linked one also carries that repository as repo (owner/name), so a reader can tell it from a pull request of the same number in the issue's own repository. For an after_merge check it is {kind: branch, branch} for the branch that issue's pull request merged into and for the repository's default branch, the default branch alone where Dispatch holds no merge of the issue. For a default_branch check it is the repository's default branch alone. Where that list is empty the check carries compared_nothing with its reason: no_pull_request_or_branch (the issue resolves to no repository, or a before_merge check's issue holds no pull request), repository_unreadable (Dispatch's GitHub App cannot read the repository) or read_failed (a read Dispatch makes did not answer). Each check also carries pass_stands {answer, roles}: yes with the roles whose passes stand, no, or unknown where the repository could not be read, and for a check CI proves whose check runs GitHub could not be read (ci state unread). A pass stands when its commit is at one of the compared commits, the check's words have not moved since it was recorded, and no retraction stands against it. Each result states two facts apart from each other. commit_stands {answer, basis, reason, repo} is where its commit stands: at_basis with the basis it matched (for a check compared with branches, the branch that carries the commit; a basis in a repository the issue links a pull request in, rather than its own, carries that repository as repo, owner/name, whether it is the head of a pull request linked there, as in compared_with, or a branch of that repository, which a result whose commit is taken to be of it is compared with), other_commit, or unknown with the reason (repository_unreadable, read_failed). An other_commit or unknown answer that a repository the issue links a pull request in decided, the one the result's commit is taken to be of, carries that repository as repo (owner/name), so a reader can tell it from an answer about the issue's own repository, which carries none. check_words_moved is whether the check's words moved after the result was recorded: true where the result's check_sha256 is not the check's digest and its check_version is not the check's version, since a check whose stored text another renderer version spelled keeps its version under a new digest. The result's own check_version stands beside the check's version. A result a retraction stands against carries retracted {reason, actor, created_at} and counts as no evidence. With no ?at=, each result also answers currency (current or older) where either word applies, for dispatch clients older than pi-envoy 17.1.0; read commit_stands, check_words_moved and retracted instead. A check CI proves is one whose ci_check names a GitHub check run, with when before_merge, no run, a negative_control, and no result recorded against it. It carries ci {run, state, case, detail, line}, read from that run at the head of the issue's open pull request of the highest number, else at the final head of its merged pull request of the highest number: state pass, fail, no_result or unread; case the conclusion that decided it (success, failure, timed_out, action_required, startup_failure, stale, or another conclusion as GitHub wrote it), or neutral, skipped, cancelled, not_completed, absent (no run of that name at the head), no_head (Dispatch holds no open or merged pull request head of the issue) or github_unreadable (state unread); detail one sentence naming the case, with GitHub's own answer where GitHub could not be read; line the pull-request body line for the check. Its one result is derived from that run on every read, for a pass or a fail alone, and is stored nowhere: id ci-run:<check run id>, role ci, actor {kind: github_app, id: the slug of the App that made the run}, session "", verdict pass or fail, commit_sha the head read, created_at the run's completed_at, observed the conclusion, the run's output title and summary cut to 2,000 runes, and its URL, one a line, check_sha256 the check's own, and no event_seq. It is compared as a recorded result is. ?at=<commit> replaces compared_with for every check of the issue by that one commit, {kind: named, commit}. The only read of GitHub it leaves is the check runs of a check CI proves, read at the issue's newest pull request head as on every read, so a derived result stands at the named commit only where that commit is that head. A value that is not 40 lowercase hex characters is 400 INVALID_QUERY. An issue with no Verification document answers no checks.

A linked pull request whose repository's name GitHub's naming rule then refuses, such as one of acme/.git, which is empty once .git is trimmed, counts for nothing and spends one of the 10 reads, and the refusal names that repository as one whose links Dispatch set aside, which no grant of the App mends. One record reads at most 10 linked pull requests, and a refusal says how many it left unread past that bound. A linked repository the App is not installed on or cannot read (GitHub's 403 that is no rate limit) does not count. A read of a linked pull request or of a linked repository that does not answer (a rate limit, a 5xx, a transport failure), where no repository is shown to hold the commit, is 502 GITHUB_UNREADABLE naming that repository, the commit and GitHub's error, and stores nothing: record the result again, after the wait a rate limit names, which Retry-After carries too. A repository the check's issue resolves to that Dispatch cannot read stores the result as before only where every linked read answered and no linked repository holds the commit: a linked read that did not answer is the 502 GITHUB_UNREADABLE above, and stores nothing. post.description: Write the status of an issue, and with an option what happens to the issues under it or above it, so that each parent's status stays in line with its children's: a parent is done only when each child is done, and while a child is in work its parent is in work. The body is {status, include_children?, unlink_children?, include_parent?, dry_run?, expected_sequence?, actor?}, and expected_sequence and actor are read as PATCH /api/v1/issues/{key} reads them. include_children writes the status on each open issue under the issue, at any depth, that is not in the status's group (not started, in work or done). unlink_children removes each open child from the issue, so that each one becomes a root. include_parent moves each ancestor that is not in work to in_progress. Each issue that an option changes gets a comment from Dispatch that names the call. When the options changed at least one issue, the issue the call names gets one comment from Dispatch too, after the last write, that names the call and lists each of those changes. The call writes one issue at a time, each in a transaction of its own, in an order where each write keeps the rule, and it checks its whole plan before the first write. The answer is 200 {issue, changed}: issue is the issue as the PATCH answers it, and changed has one entry {key, status, parent, previous_last_seq, issue} for each issue whose status or parent the call changed, the issue itself included, in the order of the writes. status and parent are what the call left, previous_last_seq is the issue's last_seq as its own write read it under its lock, and issue is that issue as its write answered it. The answer's issue is read at the issue's own write, so later events of the same call can follow it on the stored issue: a child.status for each direct child that include_children moves after it, for a status in work, and the comment.created of the comment on the issue the call names. So the stored last_seq can be past the answer's, and a client that sends the answer's last_seq as expected_sequence can get 409 ISSUE_CHANGED: it reads the issue again before a write that the sequence fences. With dry_run the call writes nothing and answers the same shape: each entry has the status and the parent that the call would leave and the issue's last_seq now, and no issue. 409 ISSUE_CHANGED: expected_sequence is not the issue's last event. This is decided first, also for a dry run, and again at each write, where an event on the issue that the call did not write stops the call. 403 LEGION_STATUS_SCOPE_REQUIRED, with an insufficient_scope challenge naming legion-status: with DISPATCH_LEGION_STATUS_SCOPE on, a step of the call writes the status of a Legion issue or moves one out from under every labelled issue, and the request's credential holds neither the person scope nor legion-status. The one exception is the owning architect's status write: a broker-issued token whose session the Legion daemon's own token published as the architect of an issue above each issue whose status the call writes, of that issue's own project, before the call and after it, writes done, backlog, icebox or triage, with neither unlink_children nor include_parent, and not done with include_children. This is decided before the first write, also for a dry run, and before PARENT_STATUS_CONFLICT. Each step's write decides it again, so a step whose issue another caller made a Legion issue after the plan stops the call there, after the steps before it. 409 PARENT_STATUS_CONFLICT {code, error, issues: [{key, title, status, relation}], changed}, relation parent or child: the call breaks the rule, with DISPATCH_PARENT_STATUS_RULE on, and for a dry run whatever the setting. 403 BROWSER_SIGN_IN_REQUIRED: include_children with done from a request that presents a token. 403 PROJECT_SCOPE: the request's credential may write one project, and a write of the call is of an issue of another project (a parent may be one), refused before any write, also for a dry run. 403 DOCUMENT_WRITER_NOT_ARCHITECT: a write of the call closes, reopens or takes out of Legion an issue Legion runs, and the session is no person, no architect of that issue or of an issue above it, and not the session of the project's Legion daemon. 400 INVALID_STATUS: the status is not in the lifecycle. 400 STATUS_CHANGE_INPUT: no status, or include_children with unlink_children. 409 PARENT_CONTENDED: the issues of the call moved at each attempt to lock them, and nothing was applied. 409 ISSUE_CLOSED: done on an issue that is closed. 404 NOT_FOUND: no such issue. Each refusal above carries changed: the entries of the writes that committed before it, [] when none did. A repeat under the same Idempotency-Key while the first call runs is 409 KEY_IN_FLIGHT, whose changed is the entries of the writes the first call has committed so far.
